title: TrueBind: A Layered Binding Defence Against Data Injection in LLM Agents
content: Language-model agents act on data written by others: an email, a bank statement, a listing. Whoever writes that data can plant a number or a fake record, and an agent that believes it pays the wrong account or reports a transaction that never happened. Today's defences ask the model to be more suspicious, and an attacker who knows the prompt writes around it. We take the decision away from the model. An attacker who writes into a record controls its words but not its structure: a planted number sits inside the text of a field, where a well-formed format keeps it. TrueBind reads every tool output into typed fields and treats the model's reply as a proposal to be checked, not an order. An action may use only a value copied from a field; a record may be chosen only when the one the user named is beyond doubt; the final answer may carry only values from a field, from the request, or from arithmetic the code can redo. Anything else is refused or withheld. The checks are plain code, so no model can be talked out of them. The attack has three forms and each layer stops one. The guarantee holds on real email, inside a working agent, against adaptive attacks and on the public benchmark for this threat, where the agent executes no planted value and keeps most of its usefulness. Where a format does not keep a stranger's text inside its field, as Markdown does not, there is nothing to bind to.
